Create three live OpenPencil concept-board pages for the newly approved GARFEX multimodal exploration. This is design mutation, but ONLY in the live OpenPencil document. Do not write/save/replace local `design.op`. If OpenPencil MCP/direct HTTP is unavailable, STOP and report; never fall back to workspace-file mutation.

Server is configured in `.mcp.json` and parent confirmed `http://127.0.0.1:3100/mcp` is live. Use direct Streamable HTTP if adapter is unavailable.

First preserve and relabel previous work (do not delete):
- page n1317 → `80 Exploración previa · Bandeja workstation`
- page n1319 → `81 Referencia previa · Bases maestras`
- page n1504 → `82 Exploración previa · Recursos`
- keep n1321 as `90 Futuro · XML y precios`

Then create 3 new pages, each with one 1440×1100 concept-board frame, and reorder them directly after pages 01–03 in this order:
1. `04A Concepto · Campo de operación`
2. `04B Concepto · Flujo continuo`
3. `04C Concepto · Intención estructurada`

COMMON BOARD CONTRACT
- Spanish visible content only.
- These are concept boards, not final components/screens.
- Same comparison structure on all three: proposition; interaction grammar; one hero mock demonstrating operation; four-experience summary; desktop/tablet/mobile mini-compositions; input-equivalence strip for mouse/touch, keyboard, voice and focus/gamepad; strengths; risks.
- Clearly show `Workspace + Command Layer + Context`.
- Use GARFEX aesthetic: `#F7F6F3`, white surfaces, text `#1F1F1D`, red `#7C0000`, yellow `#F2D031` sparingly, subtle technical lines, low fatigue, no large saturated blocks, no gamer/neon/cyberpunk styling.
- Minimum font 12px. Explicit wrapping. Keep content legible at 1440px export.
- IMPORTANT: OpenPencil smaller child index paints in front. Put all text before background shapes or otherwise guarantee correct layering.
- After each board, export actual PNG and inspect text visibility, clipping and overlaps. Fix defects.

BOARD A — CAMPO DE OPERACIÓN
Proposition: `No se entra a módulos: se activa un objeto, se revela su contexto y se decide.`
Distinct grammar: Campo; Objeto activo; Órbita contextual; Capa de comando; Foco espacial.
Hero mock: a central technical object `Cable THW-LS 2.5 mm²` connected by subtle lines to `Atributos`, `Precios`, `Origen`, `Relaciones`, with nearby work objects (`12 recursos por revisar`, `2 duplicados`, `Cotización en preparación`). Context stays anchored; command mini-layer offers Buscar/Actuar/Ver.
Four experiences summary:
- Bandeja: constelación contenida de trabajo
- Recurso: objeto técnico + relaciones
- Crear: bastidor dinámico por clasificación
- Cotizar: zona de ensamblaje
Device mini-compositions must visibly differ:
- desktop: field + fixed inspector
- tablet: field + adaptive bottom context
- mobile: prioritized object sequence
Inputs: direct select/drag alternative; arrows/Enter/Esc/CmdK; structured voice; D-pad focus/A/X/Y/B.
Strength: deep object/context identity. Risk: spatial metaphor may hurt mass review; every drag needs accessible alternative.

BOARD B — FLUJO CONTINUO
Proposition: `Una decisión clara; el siguiente paso siempre visible.`
Distinct grammar: Ahora; Después; Procesando; Focus Mode; Deshacer/continuar.
Hero mock: living vertical stream with current decision `Unidad incompatible · Cable THW-LS 2.5 mm²`, structured options `Usar m`, `Revisar equivalencias`, `Saltar`; next queue and visible processing progress. Do NOT use kanban columns or points.
Four experiences summary:
- Bandeja: corriente priorizada de decisiones
- Recurso: lectura continua con acciones
- Crear: decisión actual + resumen acumulado
- Cotizar: agregar recursos sin perder ritmo
Device mini-compositions:
- desktop: queue + context inspector
- tablet: decision surface + sliding context
- mobile: one decision, next item visible
Inputs: select/tap; arrows/Enter/Esc; voice commands that resolve structured choices; D-pad/A/B/X/Y.
Strength: exceptional focus and repetitive throughput. Risk: can hide parallel work; always offer list/context/saltar.

BOARD C — INTENCIÓN ESTRUCTURADA
Proposition: `La interfaz no conversa: compone una intención, muestra impacto y espera confirmación.`
Distinct grammar: `[acción] [entidad] [criterio] [valor] [destino]`; states Borrador/Completa/Advertencias/Lista/En proceso/Resultado.
Hero mock: instrumental command layer assembling tokens such as `[CREAR] [RECURSO] [MATERIAL ELÉCTRICO] [CONDUCTORES] [CABLE]`, then only relevant attributes `[2.5 mm²] [600 V] [NEGRO] [m]`; preview `8 de 8 decisiones · posible coincidencia`; explicit action `Revisar identidad`. Avoid chatbot bubble and CLI aesthetics.
Four experiences summary:
- Bandeja: compose what to review
- Recurso: structured search/filter intent
- Crear: classification and derived attributes
- Cotizar: intent + preview of lines/impact
Device mini-compositions:
- desktop: horizontal intent layer + workspace/context
- tablet: token bands + slide-over preview
- mobile: bottom-sheet token composition + persistent summary
Inputs: click/touch tokens; CmdK/focus movement; voice becomes editable tokens; spatial focus by regions.
Strength: strongest cross-modal parity and low manual entry. Risk: token overload/form disguised as chips; show only required arguments.

Keep every board genuinely distinct in operation and hero composition, not merely color/layout variants. Return new page/frame IDs, final page order, PNG visual-verification findings, and any known issues.

---
    name: cognitive-doc-design
    description: "Design docs that reduce cognitive load. Trigger: writing guides, READMEs, RFCs, onboarding, architecture, or review-facing docs."
    license: Apache-2.0
    metadata:
      author: gentleman-programming
      version: "1.0"
    ---
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Load this skill when creating or editing documentation that people need to understand quickly, retain, or use during review.
    
    Use it especially for:
    
    - PR descriptions and review notes.
    - Contributor or maintainer guides.
    - Architecture, workflow, or onboarding docs.
    - Any doc that currently feels long, dense, or hard to scan.
    
    ## Critical Patterns
    
    | Pattern | Rule |
    |---------|------|
    | Lead with the answer | Put the decision, action, or outcome first. Context comes after. |
    | Progressive disclosure | Start with the happy path, then add details, edge cases, and references. |
    | Chunking | Group related information into small sections. Keep flat lists short. |
    | Signposting | Use headings, labels, callouts, and summaries so readers know where they are. |
    | Recognition over recall | Prefer tables, checklists, examples, and templates over prose that must be remembered. |
    | Review empathy | Design docs so reviewers can verify intent without reconstructing the whole story. |
    
    ## Documentation Shape
    
    Use this default structure unless the repo already provides a stronger template:
    
    ```markdown
    # <Outcome-oriented title>
    
    <One paragraph: what changed, who it helps, and why it matters.>
    
    ## Quick path
    
    1. <First action>
    2. <Second action>
    3. <Verification or expected result>
    
    ## Details
    
    | Topic | Decision |
    |-------|----------|
    | <area> | <concise explanation> |
    
    ## Checklist
    
    - [ ] <Reader can confirm this>
    - [ ] <Reader can confirm that>
    
    ## Next step
    
    <Link or action that continues the workflow.>
    ```
    
    ## PR and Review Docs
    
    When documenting a PR, reduce reviewer burnout by making the review path explicit:
    
    - State what to review first.
    - State what is intentionally out of scope.
    - Link the previous and next PR when work is chained.
    - Keep each section focused on one decision or unit of work.
    - Use checklists for acceptance criteria and verification.
    
    ## Commands
    
    ```bash
    # Check markdown files changed in the current branch
    git diff --name-only -- '*.md'
    
    # Inspect PR changed-line count for cognitive load
    gh pr view <PR_NUMBER> --json additions,deletions,changedFiles
    ```
